title: Billionaire's wife back in court battling hedge fund ex after warning $633m settlement was not enough
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Billionaire's wife back in court battling hedge fund ex after warning him that $633m settlement he offered her was not enough

Laura Overdeck, 56, and her estranged husband, John Overdeck, 56, were back before a New Jersey as she seeks an even bigger slice of the fortune he built through his investment firm.

Actual Article Body:
By KELLY GARINO, US REPORTER

Published:  11:19 AEST, 7 October 2026   |  Updated:  18:15 AEST, 7 October 2026

The wife of a billionaire hedge fund manager has returned to court after rejecting a $633 million payout from her ex as the pair battle it out in New Jersey's largest divorce case.

Laura Overdeck, 56, and her estranged husband, John Overdeck, 56, were back before a judge this week as she seeks an even bigger slice of the fortune he built through his investment firm, Two Sigma.

It comes months after she rejected a settlement worth more than $600 million, claiming John had 'schemed' to leave her with as little as possible in the divorce.

Her lawyers previously claimed that he had 'methodically and strategically' tried for decades to secure his own wealth in case of a divorce, purposefully hidden his assets from his wife and 'planned his escape' during their marriage.

She is still seeking 35 percent of the value of his stake in the Manhattan-based hedge fund, which he founded with businessman David Siegel in 2001, a year before the couple married without a prenup.

But the two sides have sharply different valuations of John's stake, with his attorneys putting it at $4.5 billion and Laura's side at $6.2 billion, arguing that she is entitled to a share because it is a marital asset.

On Tuesday, the couple headed back to a Newark courtroom before family court Judge Bruce Buechler to hash out the value of Two Sigma's assets, with the firm valued at $80 billion, according to The New York Post.

John had asked the judge to clear the courtroom to keep the company's assets secret during detailed testimony from his financial expert, Todd Povlich, and won the bid.

Laura Overdeck (pictured), 56, wife of billionaire hedge fund manager John Overdeck, is seeking an even bigger slice of the fortune he built through his investment firm, Two Sigma

It comes months after she rejected a settlement worth more than $600 million, claiming John had 'schemed' to leave her with as little as possible in the divorce

Laura wants 35 percent of the value of John's stake in the Two Sigma (headquarters pictured), which he founded with businessman David Siegel in 2001, a year before the couple married without a prenup

While Judge Buechler ruled against sealing the entirety of Povlich's testimony, he ultimately agreed that portions that could reveal Two Sigma's trade secrets should be heard behind closed doors, according to the outlet.

Laura's attorneys questioned the need to keep the testimony under wraps, pointing out that John's side had already publicized its valuation of the company.

Buechler said he worried Povlich would discuss 'where the values are going, what they are looking at, what they are investing in' - details he said were protected company secrets that could hurt the firm if aired out.

During the sealed portion of the hearing, the witness was expected to detail how he arrived at his valuation of Two Sigma and explain how he valued each of the company’s 20 entities.

Laura appeared particularly engaged during the public portions of Tuesday's proceeding, sporting red sunglasses and metallic woven leather heeled mules as she typed on her laptop and repeatedly leaned over to speak with her lawyers.

Meanwhile, John appeared largely detached, spending much of his time gazing down at his cellphone as his lawyer questioned Povlich, his second-to-last witness.

It marked the 10th day of the multiday hearing over the hedge fund John co-founded with Siegel, with the two men also locked in a bitter power struggle over the company.

John had previously testified for several days, but Buechler barred Laura from taking the stand after she was accused of wrongdoing in the case, according to the New York Post.
